chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: 'Alley Cat' and Bent Fabric
summary: Wilson tells how Danish studio pianist Bent Fabricius wrote a throwaway jingle that swept the world, and links it to Hawkins's idea that plans do not decide success.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But at any rate, that type of novelty can cut through at any time, and just capture the public like that. Like sometimes I have become -- I became friendly with a good piano player in Copenhagen named Ben Fabricious; this guy was a good studio man over there and they needed a little piece of music for a radio show or a TV show in Copenhagen, and he knocked off this little thing, 'Alley Cat.' That thing swept the world, and he laughed! He's had me home to dinner in Copenhagen.
Was he the guy that wrote that?
Yeah, a studio musician. A good one. He's a studio player, composer, and his name is Ben

Fabricious -- a lot of people in Copenhagen are named Ben, B-e-n-t-. Like John, over here, Ben -- and his name is Fabricious. But they call it on the record Bent Fabric, just used the first part of it.

And he was surprised as anybody; he made so much money out of 'Alley Cat' that he bought Metro Records and years ago he recorded songs, and just recently, I got a copy of Thad Jones, a big radio band in Copenhagen playing Thad Jones, under his leadership; most of the Thad Jones music, and also some of the Danish composers -- jazz composers.
And he's flourishing with this Metro name Record label. And he never dreamed that this little jingle that he wrote for this radio and TV show would take off like it did.
And that thing cut through the rock and roll, I saw it on juke boxes all over the country.
I was going to say that that was probably the single most popular song on the club date circuit.
Oh, yeah, you always have to play 'Alley Cat' before the evening was over.
That's like what Coleman Hawkins said, he said you can't begin to plan things; he knocked that thing

out without hardly even thinking. Something that was needed quick, something that he could think of real quick, with no thought -- and his whole career was riding on something that -- He prepared himself for something else. a good studio musician. Now he's an executive, I don't know what else he's into, but it's a very successful company, the Metro home label in Copenhagen.
